svg.title: Three table cells in a row. A wide badge strip sits in the middle cell, which scrolls, so the strip's box extends well past the cell's right edge while only the part inside the cell ever paints. getBoundingClientRect reports the full box and reads as an overflow. elementFromPoint, probed inside the neighbouring cell, returns the neighbour, because nothing of the strip paints there.
svg.text: one table row, and the middle cell scrolls

g.text: getBoundingClientRect() returns the whole box, out to the dashed edge,
so the strip reads as sitting far outside its cell
elementFromPoint() at the probe returns the NEIGHBOUR, because nothing of
the strip paints there, which is the question that was actually being asked

svg.text: the rectangle is correct and the conclusion is wrong: a clipping ancestor is invisible to it
